name: candidate-routing-barrier-freshness-closure
title: Close the remaining candidate-routing barrier freshness leak and harden malformed candidate input
description: Split out from B-3f3d. Three related items remain after B-3f3d narrowed the OPEN-epoch barrier three times (F-099 evidence semantics, F-103/F-104 candidate identity, F-107 queryFiltering). (1) The candidate-routing barrier STILL leaks freshness: B-3f3d:F-107 was marked resolved on unit-level evidence only, and an end-to-end fixture then falsified it. With an unrelated commit touching only a test file, the epoch is invalidated with corpusDigest byte-identical (d49896cf->d49896cf) while candidateSpecSetDigest moves (a4cb4561->9dffdc85), so the leak is inside the candidates projection itself. Leading hypothesis: changedPaths seeds buildKeywordSeeds at weight 50 in core/candidate-spec-routing.ts:334, changing which specs are selected or their order; if only order moves, bind a sorted set of path+contentHash instead of the ordered array. A failing repro fixture already exists in the B-3f3d worktree git stash (stash@{0}) and fails CORRECTLY. (2) Malformed candidate input is unguarded: handlers/review-inventory.ts captureReviewInventoryScope does (candidates ?? []).map(...) which only guards null/undefined, so a non-array truthy candidates throws TypeError uncaught, and persistInvalidationIfDrifted has no try/catch across six gate lifecycle call sites; store.readCandidateSpecSet is a bare cast and verifyCandidateSpecSet never checks Array.isArray. (3) B-3f3d:F-108: the drift-detection call site has no end-to-end fixture proving a routing-neutral re-route does NOT invalidate.
